title: Packet glint warm-cream color is a magic literal duplicated at two draw sites; sameness enforced only by a comment
detail: The glint color and its cross-shape equality live as inline literals at two sites; retuning one silently diverges dot vs triangle glints (no unit pin). The file's own convention is named constants (CASING_OVERHANG :256, BUNDLE_EXTRA_WIDTH :247, PULSE16 :363).
recommended_fix: Hoist one named constant (e.g. PACKET_GLINT :: rl.Color{250,246,238,255}) beside CASING_OVERHANG and reference it at both call sites.

title: palette_polish_test header claims a per-channel invariant the test does not assert, and the body cites retired copper values
detail: The assertion is luminance-weighted, not per-channel; the header overstates it. The body's channel-rise example cites the retired copper (142,94,46) — under the shipped muted tiers every channel darkens, so the example is stale and misleading.
recommended_fix: Fix the header to 'darker in rec.601 luminance' and update the parenthetical to note the channel-rise rationale is now hypothetical under the muted tiers.

title: Shipped spec's frozen 'Never' clause forbids sprite regeneration, which this diff does; the spec's Change Log ships empty
evidence: spec line 35: "**Never:** No gameplay/canon-surface changes, no catalog edits, no LOG_VERSION bump, no serialization change, no sprite/asset regeneration (the committed sprite pipeline is untouched), no new node types, no pipe-color meaning change..." vs the diff's tools/gen_sprites.py: "def add_outline(name, fw, fd, base_z, scale, cx=0.0, cy=0.0):" + 12 'Binary files ... differ' sprite PNG hunks; and the spec's "## Spec Change Log" section (line 85) is empty.
detail: The spec (committed after the sprite touch-up, e38ee35) forbids what the branch already contains. The user-approved relaxation is recorded in the PR body and look-book amendment 9, but the governing spec contradicts the shipped state — drift against the project's canon/code-never-drift discipline.
recommended_fix: Record the gate-r1 sprite touch-up and the full-repolish scope ruling in the spec's Spec Change Log, citing the user gate and look-book amendment 9.
